iPhone Duo will be available for pre-order starting Friday, October 16, but scammers are trying to lure the public to visit fake websites claiming to accept orders instantly.

The malicious website is a near-perfect imitation, claiming to offer a US$500 discount voucher as an 'exclusive offer from an authorised partner'……

Cybersecurity researcher Malw網絡安全公司 Malwarebytes stated that the webpage uses the DarkSword exploit chain, which can operate on some older iPhones that have not been patched. Users do not need to perform any action—simply visiting the webpage is enough to launch the attack.

Once the attack succeeds, it will harvest identifying data and status information from the user's device, and attempt to transmit the list of installed apps and the contents of Apple Notes. Afterwards, it will turn its focus to cryptocurrency wallets.

It will then continue to attempt to access text messages, contacts, call logs, voicemail messages, emails, calendar entries, and cached location data. The malware can also contact its server to receive further instructions.

The exploit chain was publicly disclosed by Google as early as March this year, and Apple released a patch later the same month.

9to5Mac's take

The usual advice still applies—be sure to protect yourself well. Unless you trust the sender and are expecting to receive such a link, do not click on it. Be sure to install iOS updates as soon as they become available.
